- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) and price is falling, model frequently underestimates drop; add 3–8% downward bias to forecast.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to overcorrect downward; adjust upward by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates early price declines (first 5–7 days); apply 1–3% upward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is negative.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6) and price is volatile, model tends to smooth out extremes; increase forecast volatility by 10–20% to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
